chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, he said:

The sermon in the prayer for rain is before the salat, and he says seven takbirs in the first and five in the second. So this narration is anomalous, opposing the consensus of the rightful Shi'a, because their practice is upon the first narration due to its conformity with the reports that were narrated stating that salat al-istisqa' is like the salat of the two 'Ids.

key_terms.إِجْمَاعِ: consensus, here the consensus of the Shi'a community
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship
key_terms.الْخُطْبَةُ: the sermon delivered in connection with the ritual prayer
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two 'Id prayers, used here as the model for salat al-istisqa'
key_terms.شَاذَّةٌ: anomalous, irregular, and not relied upon against stronger evidence
key_terms.يُكَبِّرُ: he pronounces takbir, saying Allahu Akbar

ai.seo_question: Is the sermon in salat al-istisqa' before or after the prayer, and how many takbirs are said in it?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling concerning salat al-istisqa' and the placement of the sermon as well as the number of takbirs. It also judges one report to be anomalous because it conflicts with the consensus of the Shi'a and with other reports that liken the prayer for rain to the prayer of the two 'Ids.
